note: Scheduled Publish schedules future content-moderation transitions. It adds a field type scheduled_publish (default widget scheduled_publish, default formatter scheduled_publish_generic_formatter) whose items store value (datetime_iso8601) + moderation_state; add it to a bundle under Content Moderation, usually multi-value. A cron service scheduled_publish.update (ScheduledPublishCron::doUpdate) runs on hook_cron to apply due transitions; Drush command scheduled_publish:doUpdate (alias schp) runs it manually. Admin listing /admin/content/scheduled-publish (+ add/edit/delete), permission 'access scheduled publish pages' (listing needs view any unpublished content). No global settings form. Depends on content_moderation, workflows, datetime. Medium/hard cases are grounded in real scheduled_publish fields on the Article content type (namespaced field_sp*).

evals.prompt: How do I let editors schedule a future content-moderation state change (e.g. auto-publish next Friday) with the Scheduled Publish module? What field type do I add, and what does each entry store?
evals.expected_output: Add a field of type 'Scheduled publish' (field type id scheduled_publish) to a moderated bundle. Each entry stores a date/time (value, datetime_iso8601) and a target moderation_state; make it multi-value to queue several transitions.

evals.prompt: With the Scheduled Publish module, which Drush command runs the due scheduled moderation transitions immediately, and what normally triggers them?
evals.expected_output: Run drush scheduled_publish:doUpdate (alias schp) to apply due transitions now. Normally they run automatically on Drupal cron via the scheduled_publish.update service (ScheduledPublishCron::doUpdate).

evals.prompt: What must be true of a content type for a Scheduled Publish field to work, which permission controls the scheduled-publish admin pages, and where is the listing of pending scheduled changes?
evals.expected_output: The bundle must be under Content Moderation (in a workflow) so target moderation states exist. The 'access scheduled publish pages' permission gates the add/edit/delete forms; pending scheduled changes are listed at /admin/content/scheduled-publish (which also needs 'view any unpublished content').

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the Article content type has a field provided by the Scheduled Publish module. Inspect the live field configuration and give the machine name of the scheduled_publish field on Article.
evals.expected_output: The field is field_spx: field.storage.node.field_spx has type scheduled_publish and it is attached to the article bundle.

evals.prompt: The Article content type has a Scheduled Publish field named field_spc. Inspect the live field storage and tell me how many values (scheduled transitions) it allows.
evals.expected_output: It allows unlimited values: field.storage.node.field_spc has cardinality -1 (unlimited), so editors can queue any number of scheduled transitions.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site (Scheduled Publish is installed), add a Scheduled Publish field with machine name 'field_spt' to the Article content type so editors can schedule moderation-state changes. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: field.storage.node.field_spt exists with type scheduled_publish and a field.field.node.article.field_spt instance. E.g. FieldStorageConfig::create(['field_name'=>'field_spt','entity_type'=>'node','type'=>'scheduled_publish','cardinality'=>-1])->save(); FieldConfig::create([... 'bundle'=>'article'])->save().

evals.prompt: On the Article content type, add a Scheduled Publish field named field_spt2 that lets an editor queue MANY scheduled changes at once (not just one). Apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: field.storage.node.field_spt2 exists with type scheduled_publish and cardinality -1 (unlimited), plus a field.field.node.article.field_spt2 instance, so multiple scheduled transitions can be queued.
